chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The man is not made to swear an oath except based upon his knowledge, and the oath does not take effect except upon the knowledge, whether he has been made to swear or not.

key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: to be made to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for an oath to be valid and binding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the binding nature of an oath (yamin) is contingent upon the swearer's actual knowledge, not merely the act of swearing. This principle ensures that oaths taken in ignorance or uncertainty do not incur the penalty of perjury, emphasizing intellectual honesty in legal and religious contexts. It serves as a foundational rule for distinguishing between intentional falsehood and genuine belief in one's testimony.
